newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Thin Australian stocks climb to record close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Thin Australian stocks climb to record close.

text.p: SPI futures 2420 +9 US 30yr cl 6.54 -0.04
10yrbond futs 92.525 +0.045 Gold NY 369.45 Lon Fix 369.55
*Stocks climb to record close as Dow rises, futures expiry looms. Volumes light. Volume 215.15 million shares, value A$406.67 million, 957 stocks traded, 313 steady, 414 rises, 230 falls.
A thinly traded Australian share market climbed to a record close on Monday with a combination of end of year window dressing and futures-led trading providing most of the impetus.
By 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 17.3 points up at 2,412.9 after reaching a record intraday high of 2,416.8, surpassing the previous high of 2,408.9 which was set on November 26.
December share price index futures were up nine points at 2,420 and were at a 7.1 point premium to the underlying index.
"It looks like a bit of positive post-Christmas cheer," said a Sydney-based dealer, adding that while trade was thin in the Christmas-New Year hiatus, the rises had been widespread.
"There has been no action in the market turnover. It's certainly not busy but most of the rises are across the board."
Other players echoed these sentiments, adding that the December futures contract's retention of a modest premium augured well for Tuesday's expiry.
"It's pushed ahead rather than raced ahead but the futures look to have a lock on the premium and that should help the market hold tomorrow," said a Sydney broker.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 33 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was active ahead of the imminent December contract expiry while options trade was at a snail's pace, in line with the underlying markets.
Total options traded 17,941
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 8,481

In other local markets, Australian bond futures closed firm, helped on by further gains in U.S. Treasuries during a shortened Tokyo session ahead of the Japanese New Year holiday, which spans the rest of the week.
